title: On Tyranny: Twenty Lessons from the Twentieth Century
author: Timothy Snyder
target_audience: Students and educators of history and political science
Readers concerned with democratic values and threats to democracy
Anyone interested in learning from history to navigate current events
core_themes: Learning from the failures and successes of the twentieth century
Recognizing the early warning signs of tyranny
The role of individuals in resisting oppression
The importance of institutions, truth, and civil society
primary_purpose: To distill historical lessons from the rise of totalitarian regimes in the twentieth century into accessible, actionable advice for citizens looking to defend democracy and resist authoritarianism in contemporary society.

structure_format.organization: Divided into twenty concise chapters, each devoted to a single lesson
features: Historical examples (especially from Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union)
Calls to personal and collective action

key_concepts_lessons: Do not obey in advance: Beware of anticipatory obedience that enables authoritarianism.
Defend institutions: Stand up for core democratic processes and organizations.
Beware the one-party state: Watch for the erosion of pluralism.
Take responsibility for the face of the world: Resist the normalization of symbols of hate.
Remember professional ethics: Professionals must resist pressure to violate their codes.
Be calm when the unthinkable arrives: Authoritarians use crises to consolidate power.
Be reflective if you must be armed: Police and military should remember their duty to the people.
Stand out: Courage to stand against the crowd matters.
Be kind to our language: Avoid clichés that hide evil and resist the manipulation of language.
Believe in truth: Defend objective reality to counter propaganda.
Investigate: Seek out reliable facts and verify information.
Practice corporeal politics: Act in public, showing solidarity and visibility.
Establish a private life: Protect your privacy against intrusive power.
Contribute to good causes: Support civil society and independent organizations.
Learn from peers in other countries: Adopt best practices from those resisting tyranny elsewhere.
Listen for dangerous words: Be alert for language that legitimizes oppression.
Be as courageous as you can: Everyday resistance matters, even if small.
notable_features: Twenty standalone lessons based on historical analysis
Blend of historical narrative with practical guidance
Focused on individual agency and responsibility
Widely referenced in discussions of democratic backsliding
cultural_historical_context: Written shortly after the 2016 U.S. presidential election, in the context of international concerns about rising populism, authoritarianism, and threats to democratic norms, the book draws on Snyder’s expertise in European history to offer guidance for contemporary readers.
reception_impact: Became a bestseller, lauded for its relevance and clarity
Frequently cited in political discourse regarding threats to democracy
Used as educational material in schools and universities
Some critiques for its brevity and generalized lessons, but generally praised for accessibility and urgency
comparable_titles: How Democracies Die by Steven Levitsky and Daniel Ziblatt
The Origins of Totalitarianism by Hannah Arendt
The Road to Unfreedom by Timothy Snyder
The Anatomy of Fascism by Robert O. Paxton
